title: Colt Canada Wilson Avenue rezoning approved
subtitle: Lodging house rules, affordable housing tax exemption, renoviction advocacy, heritage designations and resident-first program registration.
overview: Council approved an official plan amendment and rezoning that change 1036, 1082 and 1094 Wilson Avenue from low-rise residential to general industrial employment for Colt Canada {{vote:m3}}. Many delegates opposed it, raising environmental effects near the Grand River, traffic safety, the loss of potential housing and the nature of weapons manufacturing. Staff noted that provincial planning rules limit what Council can consider, and that the two residential sites are vacant.

Council also approved a new Lodging House By-law, with fees and two staff positions to be dealt with in the 2025 Budget {{vote:m24}}. It agreed to a 20-year city property tax exemption for non-profit and co-operative affordable housing starting in 2025 {{vote:m25}}. It endorsed Toronto's call for stronger provincial renoviction protections {{vote:m4}}. Kitchener residents will get a seven-day head start on registering for city programs, day camps and the inclusion support worker program {{vote:m37}}.

On heritage, Council directed notices of intention to designate several properties, including a group on King Street West, and moved ahead with a revised heritage grant program. The meeting adjourned at 9:55 p.m.

decisions.detail: Council adopted an official plan amendment and approved a zoning change for 1036, 1082 and 1094 Wilson Avenue, moving the lands from low-rise residential to general industrial employment, with the amendment forwarded to the Region of Waterloo for approval.
Council approved the Lodging House By-law and its fees, and approved two full-time positions for administration, inspection and enforcement as part of the 2025 Budget.

Council agreed to join the Region's program, exempting non-profit and co-operative affordable housing providers from the city's share of property tax for 20 years from 2025, with staff to report back after the first full year.

Council endorsed Toronto's resolution urging the province to bring Bill 97 regulations into force and to amend tenant rules and Landlord and Tenant Board operations, with copies sent to provincial and municipal bodies.
Kitchener residents will be able to register for city programs, day camps and the inclusion support worker program seven days before registration opens to non-residents.
Staff were directed to finalize the revised Designated Heritage Grant Program and guidelines, with the changes to be finalized with Council as part of the 2025 Budget.

The Mayor and Clerk were authorized to sign ten-year extension agreements for public parking at 787 and 828 King Street West with the school board and at 850 King Street West with the hospital, plus a permit extension at 787 King Street West.
Council pre-approved purchase of a 2025 forestry aerial bucket truck with a budget of $255,000.
